HOW TO USE IN 3 STEPS
====================

STEP 1: IDENTIFY WHAT YOU'RE CREATING
┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Creating...             │ → Go to...
├─────────────────────────┤
│ LLM assistant           │ → agents/TEMPLATE.md
│ Proven method           │ → skills/TEMPLATE.md
│ System rule             │ → rules/TEMPLATE.md
│ Shortcut command        │ → commands/TEMPLATE.md
│ Tool/service            │ → mcps/TEMPLATE.md
│ Git automation          │ → hooks/TEMPLATE.md
│ IDE instruction         │ → instructions/TEMPLATE.md
│ Architecture decision   │ → decisions/TEMPLATE.md
│ Project guide           │ → project-docs/TEMPLATE.md
│ Lesson learned          │ → learning/TEMPLATE.md
└─────────────────────────┘

STEP 2: COPY & FILL TEMPLATE
  $ cp docs/templates/{type}/TEMPLATE.md my-artifact.md
  Then fill in the placeholders

STEP 3: VALIDATE & COMMIT
  $ scripts/validate-{type}.sh my-artifact.md  (once available)
  $ git commit -m "feat(artifacts): add {name}"

TOTAL TIME: 25-50 minutes per artifact

GLOBAL RULES (APPLY TO ALL)
===========================

1. ENGLISH ONLY
   → All code, comments, docs in English

2. NO DUPLICATION
   → Each artifact defined once, everywhere else link to it

3. CLEAR DEPRECATION
   → If removing artifact, announce in 2-week notice

4. TESTABLE EXAMPLES
   → All examples must be real and working

5. CONTEXT LIMITS
   → No single artifact > 150 lines (split if larger)

6. METADATA CONSISTENCY
   → All functional artifacts include id/name, version, keywords

VALIDATION CHECKLIST (QUICK)
=============================

Before committing artifact:
  ☐ Template copied and filled
  ☐ All placeholders replaced with real content
  ☐ Examples are working (tested locally)
  ☐ Follows applicable global rules
  ☐ Read and followed GUIDE-DO-DONT.md (if exists)
  ☐ Links to related artifacts added
  ☐ Metadata (keywords, id) filled in
  ☐ No hardcoded config values

All checked? → Ready to commit!

CLOSING THOUGHT
===============

This template system represents a shift from:

  ❌ "How do I create a [thing]?" → Search docs, guess format
  ❌ "What's good?" → Look at old examples, hope they're good
  ❌ "Let me document this" → Freeform, whatever

To:

  ✅ "How do I create a [thing]?" → Copy template, fill, validate
  ✅ "What's good?" → Follow 8+ tested best practices
  ✅ "Let me document this" → Use template, structured, consistent

All templates are ready NOW.
Team can start using TODAY.
System scales as you grow.
